name: Moses
charge: Refusing to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; faithful in all the Lord’s house; very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth
summary: Things were not bad for Moses in Egypt; he made them bad for himself by choosing his people. By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter, chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasures of sin for a season, and led a stiffnecked house forty years. The Lord’s testimony on him is unmatched: his servant Moses was faithful in all his house, and he spoke with him mouth to mouth. He was very meek, above all the men on the face of the earth, and God buried him.
offenseFull: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt, for he had respect to the recompence of the reward (Hebrews 11:24-26). Everybody in ancient Egypt was not badly off. Some of our people had money and standing and were comfortable with the oppression they lived under, like the officers of the children of Israel whom the taskmasters had set over their own brethren, until the beatings came to them too (Exodus 5:14); the same men live in spiritual Egypt now. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and his customs Egyptian, and he laid every bit of it down to be what he was called to be.

He was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds (Acts 7:22). He did not stutter, as is commonly taught; he was not fluent in the Hebrew of his brethren, having been raised in Pharaoh’s court and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years, so Aaron was given him for a mouth and he stood to Aaron instead of God (Exodus 4:10-16). From the royal court he went to keeping his father in law’s flock for forty years, and when the Lord called him out of the bush his answer was, who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh (Exodus 3:11). A man’s goings are of the Lord (Proverbs 20:24). He built the tabernacle exactly as the Lord commanded him (Exodus 40:16), bore a congregation that murmured at every stage, and stood between the people and the wrath they provoked, asking to be blotted out of the Lord’s book if their sin was not forgiven (Exodus 32:11-14, 32). The man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3).
judgmentFull: When Miriam and Aaron spoke against him because of the Ethiopian woman, who was Zipporah the daughter of the priest of Midian, and asked whether the Lord had spoken only by Moses and not also by them, the Lord heard it, came down in the pillar of the cloud, and declared the difference: to a prophet among them he would make himself known in a vision and speak in a dream, but his servant Moses was not so, being faithful in all his house; with him he would speak mouth to mouth, even apparently and not in dark speeches, and Moses beheld the similitude of the Lord; why then were they not afraid to speak against his servant (Numbers 12:1-8). They that despise government and speak evil of dignities are presumptuous and selfwilled (2 Peter 2:10). Miriam became leprous, white as snow, and was shut out of the camp seven days, and the people did not journey until she was brought in again. The Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (Exodus 33:11).

He was refused the land for Meribah, which is entered separately, and the Lord buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, and no man knows of his sepulchre to this day (Deuteronomy 34:5-6). He was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, and his eye was not dim nor his natural force abated (Deuteronomy 34:7): he was not a weak, sickly old man; he was in full strength, and still he had to go up and die, because he could not enter. There arose not a prophet since in Israel like him, whom the Lord knew face to face (Deuteronomy 34:10). That verse also answers a doctrine. Some say Joshua was the prophet raised up like Moses, and therefore there is no Christ; but the same passage that says Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom says in the next breath that there arose not a prophet like Moses. Joshua was a mighty prophet, and he did not fit that word; Christ did (Deuteronomy 18:18). And Moses himself stood on the mount with Elijah at the transfiguration (Matthew 17:3).

text.text: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?
And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
And Moses said unto the Lord, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
And the Lord said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the Lord?
Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
And he said, O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.

And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
And thou shalt speak unto him, and put words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.
And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?
Thus did Moses: according to all that the Lord commanded him, so did he.
And Moses besought the Lord his God, and said, Lord, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand?

Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self, and saidst unto them, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.
And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.
Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.
(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)
And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said, Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.
(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)
And the Lord spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.
And the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.

And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.
So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.
And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth–peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.
And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said, Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.
